chunks: And from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: Allah, the Exalted, said:

By My Honor! I do not take a servant of Mine from the world if I intend mercy for him, until I have fully accounted for all his sins—either by straitening his livelihood, or by an affliction in his body, or by a fear that I cause him to experience. And if anything remains of his sins, I make his death difficult.

And he (peace be upon him) said: Allah also said: By My Honor! If I intend to chastise a servant of Mine, I do not take him from the world until I have fully compensated him for all his good deeds—either by increasing his livelihood, or by health in his body, or by a sense of security that I cause him to experience. And if anything remains of his good deeds, I make his death easy.
ai.seo_question: How does Allah expiate a believer's sins in this world?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the divine mechanism of accounting for sins and good deeds through worldly trials and ease. For those destined for mercy, sins are expiated through hardship, poverty, illness, or fear, with difficult death if any remain; for those destined for chastisement, good deeds are compensated through ease, health, and security, with easy death if any remain.

en.muhajir-b-ali: 12. It has been narrated that Abu Ja'far (al-Baqir) (a.s) said: Allah [M.G] has said:

By My Honor! I do not take a servant of Mine from the world, if I intend mercy for him, until all his sins are removed—either by a straitening in his livelihood, by an affliction in his body or a fear that I cause him to experience. And if anything remains on him thereafter, I make his dying difficult.

Abu Ja'far (a.s) also said: Allah has also said: By My Honor! If I intend to chastise a servant of Mine, I do not take him from the world until I compensate him fully for his good deeds—either by increasing his livelihood, by health in his body or by a sense of security that I cause him to experience. And if anything remains for him thereafter, I make his dying easy.
